# TDPdf v1.29.6.0

**Bold/Italic buttons for placed and edited text, and a round of fixes to the text style bar found through real hands-on testing — a mid-edit style change that silently didn't apply, a style-only edit to existing PDF text that got discarded, the style bar not showing up for Edit Existing Text, illegible toggle buttons, a hardcoded black background, a missing horizontal scrollbar in Grid view, a startup crash on a corrupted settings file, and a UI freeze on text commit.**

## Bold and Italic buttons

Character styling already worked end-to-end — Ctrl+B/Ctrl+I while actively typing set it, and it rendered, saved, and survived undo correctly. There was just no button for it. The text style bar now has real Bold and Italic toggles next to Font and Size.

## Style changes now actually apply while you're still editing

This release is mostly the result of testing that specifically tried to break the style bar, and it found a real, structural bug: none of Font, Size, Color, Bold, or Italic ever updated the text box you were currently editing — only the *next* box's defaults. Only the whiteout-fill toggle had ever been wired to update a box live. All five now do.

For Edit Existing Text specifically, it was worse: even a style-only change (recoloring text without touching the wording) was silently thrown away, because the commit path treated "the text didn't change" as "nothing changed" and skipped applying anything else — and when it didn't skip, it rebuilt the saved result from the *original* detected style rather than what was actually set. Both are fixed, and the style bar itself now correctly shows up for that tool at all, which it previously didn't outside of very specific moments.

## The disappearing-and-reappearing style bar, explained

Clicking a real, focusable control in the style bar — Font, Size, Bold, Italic — took keyboard focus away from the text box you were editing, and losing focus was already the app's signal that you'd clicked away and were done. So adjusting a style mid-edit silently ended the edit early. The box would then get selected, and its selection highlight (a translucent green tint) wrapping a short piece of text looked like the whole box had turned green. The style bar is now correctly treated as part of the same edit.

## Smaller fixes along the way

- The new Bold/Italic buttons — and, once we went looking, the Shape tool's existing rectangle/ellipse/line/polygon buttons too — rendered as illegible solid blocks. Both now use the app's real button styling.
- The text and shape style bars had a hardcoded near-black background instead of a theme color. Now matches the rest of the UI.
- Grid view had no horizontal scrollbar, so a page rendered wider than a shrunk window at high zoom clipped content with no way to reach it.
- A corrupted settings file (`user.config`) could crash the app on launch even after the app's own self-heal ran — a .NET quirk meant the very next settings read after the heal could still fail. Found via fleet telemetry.
- Committing certain text could freeze the app for about a second, with clicks made during the freeze appearing to do nothing until several queued up and fired at once. A font-coverage check was reading a font file from disk synchronously on the UI thread; it now runs in the background.
